svg.text: 10 · The AWS side: one account, one app user, least privilege
Every AWS service the app uses, who may call it, and what each permission allows. Region ap-southeast-2 (Sydney)
AWS account (mine) · root signs in with MFA (passkey), never used by the app
the app's only identity on AWS
its access key lives only in Fly secrets,
never in the repo or in chat
covers the Converse API; no admin calls
no EC2, Route 53, IAM or billing actions
no other bucket; no console sign-in
a leaked key can upload, email or ask a
model, but cannot build or delete servers
Set up by hand, as me
EC2, Elastic IP, Route 53 records, SES domain,
the bucket's 30-day rule and the budget:
done in the console, not by the app
browser reaches it only by a 5-minute
Amazon Nova 2 Lite: the rest, and turning
the app's own limit (50 a day per assistant)
is the only real cap on the bill
monthly budget with e-mail alerts to me
alerts only: on the free tier there is
no automatic stop, so the server's daily
limits are what keep spending small
443 TCP (TLS, signalling, TURN/TLS) · 80 TCP (certificates) · 7881 TCP (WebRTC fallback)
3478 UDP (TURN) · 50000–60000 UDP (audio) · 22 TCP from my IP only · 7880 stays closed (behind Caddy)
The app server never calls EC2: it signs tickets with the LiveKit secret, kept in Fly secrets.
The Fly machine sits outside AWS and calls it with this one user's key.
